caption.text: Part 3 of LINUX PERMISSIONS: A FIELD HANDBOOK. chmod -R 777 is not a fix, it is a confession. This handbook walks the whole Linux permission model end to end — the nine bits, why x on a directory means search and not execute, octal by hand, umask as a bit-clear rather than a subtraction, setuid, the sticky bit, POSIX ACLs and their mask trap, and the exact order the kernel checks. Ten pages of dense field notes, including the three questions that diagnose nearly every permission bug.
